name: Neck Flexion and Extension (Plate or Harness)
summary: Loaded neck flexion and extension using a plate or a neck harness to strengthen the muscles at the front and back of the neck. Keep the load very light and the movement slow.
setup: Start with very light weight or just a folded towel and plate, well below what you think you can handle.
Sit or lie on a bench with a stable position and a neutral spine.
Attach the harness or place the plate carefully, with a spotter or hands ready if needed.
Warm up the neck with gentle movement first.
execution: Lower the head slowly through a small, comfortable range.
Raise the head back to neutral, keeping the movement slow and controlled.
Pause briefly, then repeat for 10-15 reps with strict control.
Add weight in tiny steps, only when every rep is smooth and pain-free. Stop at once if you feel dizzy, numb, tingling or sharp pain.
mistakes: Using too much weight too soon: begin with very light loads and progress gradually over weeks.
Jerking or bouncing the head: use a slow tempo.
Going into extreme range: stay within a comfortable range.
Ignoring warning signs such as dizziness, numbness or tingling: stop the exercise immediately and consult a professional.
